evidence.claim: Georgia DOT describes gently undulating terrain and opportunities to explore cultural and natural attractions beyond the interstate, including Pine Mountain and Franklin Delano Roosevelt State Park.

Rich cultural and natural attractions may be found in the vicinity of the Byway, such as Pine Mountain and Franklin Delano Roosevelt State Park.

evidence.claim: A life-size sculpture of Franklin Roosevelt marks the overlook at Dowdell’s Knob in F.D. Roosevelt State Park.
evidence.quote: Above King’s Gap is Dowdell’s Knob where President Franklin D. Roosevelt sometimes picnicked and pondered world affairs. A life-size sculpture of the president now welcomes visitors to the overlook.

flags: Construction chronology conflicts: the corridor plan gives September 1964 to February 1981; the Interstate article describes construction in 1966 and full opening in 1979. Omitted construction dates.
Use current Georgia DOT’s 38-mile byway length; the 2007 plan says approximately 39 miles. The full interstate is a different extent.
Pine Mountain’s Appalachian relationship is inconsistent within the plan and with the park article. Dropped the southernmost-mountain-country claim and avoided that classification.
Goat Rock fault remains a short moment because the cache gives only a location and a view, without geological explanation or a stopping place. No pull-off is implied.

Dowdell’s Knob is an off-interstate excursion grouped with the ridge before the southward approach to Muscogee County. The plan has erroneous west/east descriptions of Pine Mountain; no such directions are reused.
Park acreages differ across sources; omitted. No driving time is supported.
Application approval in summer 2006 is distinguished from byway status granted in 2007. Fault visibility rests on the 2007 plan, not a recent field observation.
